subject: Vector economics & dimension eligibility — pricing and commitment options
messages:
From: Alice Chen <alice@searchlytics.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 2 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Vector pricing baseline + model eligibility

Hi Dylan,

We're kicking off an evaluation of embeddings for a new semantic search product and I need a clear baseline to present to our engineering and procurement teams. A few specific asks: 

- Do you price embeddings per-vector or per-token? We currently index ~10M vectors/month (mostly 1536-dim), and need a baseline cost estimate.
- Are certain dimension sizes (768/1536/3072) priced differently? If so, what's the multiplier or effective rate for each bucket?
- Which embedding models are eligible for hosted pricing? We care about multilingual support (en, es, pt) and prefer open models, but would consider Redwood-verified ones if the economics are right.
- Do you have an enterprise discount schedule for volume / committed spend?

I've attached a small sample of document IDs (searchlytics_sample_ids.csv) so we can discuss sample evaluations. Can we get a short ratecard and an outline of any commitment options?

Thanks,
Alice Chen
Head of ML — Searchlytics
alice@searchlytics.com

---
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice@searchlytics.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Sep 2025 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Vector pricing baseline + model eligibility

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear asks and the sample. Quick answers up front, then details and options: 

1) Billing unit: embeddings are billed per-vector for the hosted API (not per-token). Generation APIs are per-token; we keep the units separate to avoid confusion.

2) Dimension tiers: our standard baseline is quoted against a 1536-dim profile (Redwood-embed-1536). Pricing multipliers we use internally: 768-dim = 0.55x, 1536-dim = 1.0x, 3072-dim = 1.9x. For very custom dims we map to the nearest tier.

3) Model eligibility: hosted pricing covers Redwood-verified embeddings (1536/3072 variants) plus a curated set of community/open models (Open-Embed-768, m-embed-multilingual). Some experimental open models are allowed but require a compatibility check. Multilingual is supported by m-embed-multilingual and Redwood-embed-1536-ml.

4) Discounts & commitments: we typically offer volume tiers and annual committed packs. Example baseline: $0.00022/vector at 1536-dim for pay-as-you-go. Commit examples: 12-mo commit for 10M vectors/month -> blended $0.00015/vector (20% discount + pack credits); 24-mo larger commits available.

I've attached a draft ratecard (redwood-embed-ratecard-q3.pdf) and a one-page commitment summary. Would you be open to a 30-minute call Thursday to review tradeoffs (cost vs latency vs model selection) and discuss a short eval window?

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Dylan — really helpful, thanks. A couple of follow-ups: 

- Quality vs dims: if we move from 1536 -> 768 to save cost, what typical drop in retrieval relevance should we expect? Any internal evals or published curves?
- For the hosted Redwood-verified models, do you expose model version pins? We need deterministic behavior for ops reproducibility.
- The baseline numbers look reasonable — can you confirm if the $0.00022/vector is per-API-call (i.e., per embedding generated) or per stored vector once ingested? Our workflow both generates embeddings and stores them; we need to model both write and read costs.

Also Tom (CC) will be handling procurement questions — looping him in. 

Thanks,
Alice

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice@searchlytics.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Sep 2025 17:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Vector pricing baseline + model eligibility

Hi Alice — jumping in from Commercial. Short answers: 

- Quality curves: we have an internal benchmark set across representative retrieval tasks; typical delta from 1536->768 is ~3–7% relative MAP drop depending on domain. We'll share a short figure on the call; exact impact depends on your corpus and fine-tuning.
- Model pins: yes, hosted endpoints can be pinned to model versions and we provide release notes for each model variant. Customers can request long-term pinning with a version-guard SLA.
- Billing clarifications: the per-vector line item covers embedding generation (API call). Storage/ingestion is not billed as a repeating vector cost in the hosted plan — you pay once per vector generated; additional reads/queries do not incur per-vector charges (they incur search/query API charges if you use our managed search). If you export and re-ingest, generation charge applies again.

Commit constructs: for a 10M vector/month baseline we recommend a 12-month committed pack (Searchlytics-10M) with quarterly true-ups — that gives you predictable unit economics and priority capacity. I've attached a draft SOW (SOW-searchlytics-draft.docx) with the proposed commitment language and SLAs.

Next steps I propose: 1) 30-min scoping call with engineering to confirm sample eval, 2) 48-hour trial credit for 50k vectors so you can validate quality/latency on your set, 3) draft commercial term sheet for procurement to review.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Director, Commercial | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachments: SOW-searchlytics-draft.docx (Word, 3 pages)
